policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'And I answered him' is first person, matching the qere 1cs form vaomar; the ketiv vayyomer would be 'and he said' (3ms), which the English excludes.
ASV 'his clothes, and rent them' is plural, matching the qere bivgadav (plural with suffix); the ketiv bevigdo 'his garment' is singular, which the English excludes.

ASV 'Thy blood' does not distinguish singular damekha (qere) from plural damekha (ketiv); English 'blood' is a mass noun that regularly renders Hebrew plural damim, and no ASV note is mapped to this unit. Base qere fallback retained.
